summary.intent: Make the built-in type checker the default across Caliper (accepting some loss of timing lead), land a fix for a snapshot leak in PR #440, and decide whether to clean up the Go tsgo beta work.
summary.outcome: The default flip (S8, branch feat/checker-is-default) was delegated to a worker and is still running. PR #440 got the snapshot-leak fix at 10df5137, verified on the remote. The user agreed to remove the tsgo beta plumbing from the product while keeping the oracle copy, as slice 4 of #369, queued behind S8.

repo: The Go checker (typescript@7.1.0-beta) is kept only in apps/oracle as an independent judge of tsrs. It supplies the construct-suite goldens (~228 rows), the construct:parity gate, and the weekly oracle arbiter. Without it tsrs would judge itself, and a regression would look like a changed golden.

Product-side tsgo plumbing slated for deletion in slice 4 of #369: crates/tsc-client, crates/semantic/src/locate.rs, record_fixture.rs, the version recognition in semantic/src/lib.rs, the project typescript@beta fallback (trail #368), and the two ci.yml jobs setting CALIPER_TEST_TSC.

After slice 4, Rust tests use the built-in checker. CALIPER_TEST_TSC points at the Go beta only in the two tests that need it, and the packaging check should compare the oracle's npm tsrs pin with the Cargo pin.

The default flip renames the opt-in --experimental-semantic-types / semanticTypes to --no-checker (structural resolver). --tsc-path still selects the process route. The rename is breaking and needs a changeset.

Whole-project extract had an answer-cache problem: 5.5 MiB per Chakra component reached over 5 GB at 900 components. It must be fixed or explained before the default ships. Measurements go in docs/gate-measurements.md.
The 150 ms budget stays for prefetched or cached stories. The cold first answer (171 ms) and the ButtonProps watch p95 (162 ms) are recorded as measured.

The snapshot leak was fixed in crates/semantic/src/checker.rs: refused createSnapshot/updateSnapshot requests and callers that stopped waiting now release their snapshots. Sibling leaks were fixed in on_demand.rs and rpc.rs.
The --tsc-path process route has the same caller-timeout leak but is bounded, because a process is replaced after 64 programs.
The oracle is not run by the flip worker; it stays a single run after the merge.

code.finding: Refused createSnapshot/updateSnapshot now release the snapshot the request made, and snapshots for callers past their deadline are released through a new discard method. Tests: a_snapshot_made_by_a_refused_request_is_released_and_the_ones_answered_are_kept and a_snapshot_made_after_its_caller_stopped_waiting_is_released.
A fatal error while updating the kept snapshot used to drop it without releasing it; it is now released.
A createSnapshot answer with no project returned an error and left its snapshot held; it is now released first.

workflow: After a subagent reports a push, verify with git ls-remote. An earlier #440 push went out from the wrong local branch because git checkout -b failed silently, so the PR showed no diff.
Use git push origin HEAD:<branch> and verify the remote hash when worktree branch names are uncertain.
Serialize workers that touch the same files (S8 and slice 4 both edit semantic/lib.rs and the CLI/napi options) to avoid merge conflicts.
The Entire Gates finding stays open until Entire re-checks the new commit, so recheck later rather than assuming the fix failed.
Test the leak fix with a release-check assertion on snapshot ids rather than by measuring arena growth.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions or approval.

friction: The first #440 push went out from the wrong local branch because git checkout -b failed, so the PR showed no diff.
A clippy type_complexity error appeared in the new test and needed a fix after the first lint run.
just deny, just semver and just test-checker-lane were not re-run after the test-only lint fix.
PR #440 shows BLOCKED on Entire Gates only, with no failing checks, because the finding still reads open until Entire re-checks.
#440 shares some docs with the default flip, so the worker has to keep its doc edits in separate hunks and merge main before the final push.
open_items: Wait for the S8 worker (feat/checker-is-default) to report, then link its trail and write the PR body.
Start slice 4 of #369 (remove the product-side tsgo beta plumbing) after S8 merges.
Recheck the Entire finding on PR #440 after the new commit is evaluated.
Run the oracle once after the default flip merges.
Decide whether to shrink the Go-based oracle to just construct:parity and the goldens if the weekly run does not need the rest.
Leave the --tsc-path process-route caller-timeout leak unfixed for now, since it is bounded by the 64-program process replacement.
Re-run just deny, just semver and just test-checker-lane on the final #440 tree.
